intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1A) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding the mineralocorticoid receptor (NR3C2; 600983) on chromosome 4q31.23.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1A) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene NR3C2.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that hMR mutations are a common feature of autosomal dominant PHA1, being found in 70% of our familial cases.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports heterozygous hMR mutations in autosomal dominant PHA1. NR3C2 is the approved symbol for hMR.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 gene, which encodes the mineralocorticoid receptor, is located on chromosome 4q31.23.

checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature restating the MR gene; not stated in the abstract itself.

paragraphs.text: Pseudohypoaldosteronism type I (PHA1) is a primary form of mineralocorticoid resistance. It presents in the newborn with renal salt wasting, dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis and failure to thrive, despite elevated plasma aldosterone and plasma renin activity (Geller et al., 1998; Tajima et al., 2000; Pujo et al., 2007). The autosomal dominant or sporadic form, caused by inactivating mutations in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene, has milder salt wasting that improves with age. The autosomal recessive form is severe, affects multiple organs, and persists into adulthood (Geller et al., 1998; Tajima et al., 2000; Pujo et al., 2007).

checks.evidence_quote: Type 1 pseudohypoaldosteronism (PHA1) is a primary form of mineralocorticoid resistance

checks.evidence_quote: PHA1) is a rare condition characterized by neonatal salt loss with dehydration, hypotension, hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis
checks.explanation: Failure to thrive is not mentioned in the abstract.

checks.claim: In newborns with PHA1, plasma aldosterone and plasma renin activity are elevated.
checks.evidence_quote: despite elevated plasma aldosterone levels and PRA

checks.claim: The autosomal dominant or sporadic form of PHA1 is caused by inactivating mutations in the mineralocorticoid receptor gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Inactivating mutations of the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR; NR3C2) are responsible for autosomal dominant and some sporadic cases of PHA1.

checks.claim: The autosomal dominant or sporadic form of PHA1 has milder salt wasting that improves with age.
checks.evidence_quote: an autosomal dominant PHA1 manifests milder salt wasting that gradually improves with advancing age

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of PHA1 is severe, affects multiple organs, and persists into adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: An autosomal recessive form manifests severe life-long salt wasting resulting from multiple mineralocorticoid target tissue such as sweat, salivary glands, the colonic epithelium, and lung.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes severe life-long salt wasting from multiple mineralocorticoid target tissues. 'Persists into adulthood' is a reasonable reading of 'life-long', but the claim's 'severe' and 'affects multiple organs' are not stated in those words.

paragraphs.text: Armanini et al. (1985) studied 3 patients with pseudohypoaldosteronism. One was a 28-year-old index case from Melbourne. The other 2 were sibs from Munich, aged 8 and 2 years, whose parents were first cousins. The younger sib, a boy, was less severely affected than his sister. The authors described the syndrome as salt wasting and failure to thrive, usually presenting in infancy. Urinary sodium was high despite hyponatremia, and patients had hyperkalemia, hyperreninemia, and elevated aldosterone levels.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) described a kindred (kindred I) with type I pseudohypoaldosteronism. The propositus presented in infancy with renal salt wasting, vomiting, failure to thrive, short stature, hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia. She responded dramatically to a high-salt diet (2.5 g/day), and sodium supplementation was stopped at age 2 years. Seven additional family members from 3 generations were affected, with clinical expression ranging from asymptomatic to moderate.

paragraphs.text: Armanini et al. (1985) found that Percoll-separated monocytes from controls bound [3H]aldosterone with high affinity (Kd about 3 nM) and limited capacity (150 to 600 sites per cell). On repeated testing, monocytes from patients 1 and 2 showed no [3H]aldosterone binding. Patient 3, who was less severely affected, had 62 sites per cell, more than 2 SD below the control level. The parents of the Munich sibs had normal levels. The authors concluded that pseudohypoaldosteronism is caused by a type I (mineralocorticoid) receptor defect, which may be complete or partial.

paragraphs.text: Hanukoglu (1991) described a second kindred in which the propositus was the child of a consanguineous marriage. She developed severe renal salt losing at age 9 days, with raised salivary and sweat electrolytes, indicating that multiple target organs did not respond to mineralocorticoids. Life-threatening salt wasting recurred after age 2 years, and at 5 years she needed 14 g/day of salt. A sister died at 9 days with PHA symptoms. The pedigree was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. From these kindreds and the literature, Hanukoglu (1991) concluded that type I PHA consists of 2 clinically and genetically distinct entities, one with a renal defect and one with defects in multiple target organs.

paragraphs.text: Riepe et al. (2006) identified 6 different heterozygous NR3C2 mutations in 6 patients with PHA1. These comprised a previously reported frameshift (c.1131dupT), a second frameshift (c.2871dupC), 2 novel nonsense mutations producing a truncated receptor, and 2 missense mutations (S818L and E972G). Functional studies showed that the c.2871dupC, S818L, and E972G mutants had absent or markedly reduced aldosterone binding and transactivation. The authors concluded that their data extended the spectrum of PHA1-causing NR3C2 mutations.

paragraphs.text: Pujo et al. (2007) carried out a comprehensive screen of the MR gene in patients with PHA1. They searched the coding regions, intron-exon junctions, and untranslated exons for nucleotide substitutions, and also looked for large deletions. They found 22 MR gene abnormalities in 33 patients. The authors concluded that MR mutations are extremely frequent in PHA1 patients classified according to aldosterone and potassium levels.

checks.claim: Pujo et al. (2007) screened the MR gene coding regions, intron-exon junctions, and untranslated exons for nucleotide substitutions in patients with PHA1.
checks.evidence_quote: We present the first comprehensive study seeking nucleotide substitutions in coding regions, intron-exon junctions, and untranslated exons

checks.claim: Pujo et al. (2007) also searched for large deletions in the MR gene in patients with PHA1.
checks.evidence_quote: as well as for large deletions

checks.claim: Pujo et al. (2007) found 22 MR gene abnormalities in 33 PHA1 patients.
checks.evidence_quote: A total of 22 MR gene abnormalities were found in 33 patients.

checks.claim: Pujo et al. (2007) concluded that MR mutations are extremely frequent in PHA1 patients classified according to aldosterone and potassium levels.
checks.evidence_quote: We demonstrate that MR mutations are extremely frequent in PHA1 patients classified according to aldosterone and potassium levels

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a Japanese family with a renal form of PHA1, Tajima et al. (2000) used PCR and direct sequencing to identify a heterozygous mutation in the NR3C2 gene. The mutation changed codon 924 from CTG to CCG, resulting in a leu924-to-pro (L924P) substitution. COS-1 cells were transfected with a GRE-tk-CAT reporter. Aldosterone increased CAT activity with the wildtype receptor but had no effect with the L924P mutant. The authors suggested that this missense mutation caused the mineralocorticoid resistance in the family.

checks.claim: Tajima et al. (2000) used PCR and direct sequencing to identify a heterozygous NR3C2 mutation in affected members of a Japanese family with a renal form of PHA1.
checks.evidence_quote: PCR and direct sequencing of the MR gene identified a heterozygous point mutation changing codon 924 Leu (CTG) to CCG (Pro) (L924P) in all affected members.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 mutation in the Japanese PHA1 family changed codon 924 from CTG to CCG, resulting in a leu924-to-pro (L924P) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: changing codon 924 Leu (CTG) to CCG (Pro) (L924P)

checks.claim: Tajima et al. (2000) transfected COS-1 cells with a GRE-tk-CAT reporter to test NR3C2 L924P function.
checks.evidence_quote: COS-1 cells were transfected with expression vectors for either wild type or the mutant MR-L924P receptors, together with the reporter plasmid (glucocorticoid response element tk-CAT).

checks.claim: In COS-1 cells, aldosterone increased CAT activity with the wildtype mineralocorticoid receptor.
checks.evidence_quote: Aldosterone increased CAT activity in cells expressing wild-type receptor

checks.claim: In COS-1 cells, aldosterone had no effect on CAT activity with the NR3C2 L924P mutant.
checks.evidence_quote: but had no effect in cells expressing the mutant receptors

checks.evidence_quote: These results suggest that mineralocorticoid resistance in this family is due to a missense mutation in the MR gene.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with sporadic PHA I, Viemann et al. (2001) identified a frameshift mutation, an insertion of C at nucleotide 2871 (Ins2871C), in exon 9 of the NR3C2 gene. The mutation was absent in the patient's asymptomatic family members. It was the first mutation described in exon 9 and affects the last 27 amino acids of the hormone-binding domain.

checks.evidence_quote: We here report the results of a genetic study in a sporadic case
checks.explanation: The abstract states that the study included a sporadic case.

checks.claim: In a patient with sporadic PHA I, a frameshift mutation, an insertion of C at nucleotide 2871 (Ins2871C), was identified in exon 9 of the NR3C2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: In the sporadic case we identified a new frameshift mutation, Ins2871C, in exon 9 of the hMR gene.
checks.explanation: hMR is the human mineralocorticoid receptor, whose approved gene symbol is NR3C2. 'Ins2871C' is the same variant as an insertion of C at nucleotide 2871.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 Ins2871C mutation was absent in the asymptomatic family members of the patient with sporadic PHA I.

checks.claim: The NR3C2 Ins2871C mutation affects the last 27 amino acids of the hormone-binding domain.

checks.explanation: The paper says 'impairs' and the draft says 'affects'. The meaning is essentially the same.
